item.title: Aaron Judge, the Yankees rotation and four playoff series worth watching and wagering on this week
item.description: Four playoff series begin with up to 22 games before the World Series, as the White Sox, Yankees, Braves, and Padres enter as betting favorites.
item.content:encoded:
There are as many as 22 games remaining if a team goes to the World Series, and the distance in every series, to end the 2026 season.

If you don't tune into playoff baseball, you're missing out. A lot of people, myself included, praise the NHL for having a great postseason, but baseball might be just as good. There are more pitching decisions and matchups, and the importance of every pitch is magnified. We have four series starting today and I think we can put some wagers on the full games.

This might be the poster year for why baseball should change the postseason format. We have the Astros barely making the playoffs with a .500 record, and they get to host a series, while the White Sox, who finished three games ahead of the Astros, have to travel to Houston to play them. The Astros have the experience and a potential MVP in Yordan Alvarez. Their offense is almost certainly better than the White Sox. In terms of pitching matchups, I think it is fairly close. This will come down to whichever team is less likely to make a mistake. The Astros are 5-2 against the White Sox this year. I think the White Sox, even with their inexperience, are in a better spot to win the series. The Astros have shown they are an average team all year long. I like the White Sox to win, and I like this series to go 3 games.

PHILLIES AVOID COLLAPSE, ASTROS SNEAK IN AS MLB POSTSEASON IS SET

Another chapter in the storied histories of these two clubs. The Red Sox have been one of the hottest teams in baseball for the past few months. The Yankees have been consistent all season. Offensively, the series may hinge on how well Ben Rice will do. Aaron Judge is unlikely to play in the series, but New York has played well without him. The Red Sox seem to have a bit more of a balanced offense. I think the pitching edge comes on the Yankees side. They have the likely Cy Young winner going in Game 1, then they can send out Max Fried, and finally Gerrit Cole for their three starters. The Red Sox have a team ERA about the same as the Yankees, but Sonny Gray is really the only guy I consistently trust. I like the Yankees, but I won't personally play the -170 on them.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Atlanta Braves host the Philadelphia Phillies, and this is a very similar series to the Yankees and Red Sox. The Braves were consistent all year, and the Phillies showed stretches of being great and others where they were a little less impressive. Philadelphia has the rotation, but because of how this season went for them, I would guess they have to start Jesus Luzardo first, but he pitched in relief yesterday. Ideally, they send Christopher Sanchez, then Zack Wheeler, and then Luzardo if needed.

Because they needed to fight for their spot until the last day of the season, it likely won't line up that way. The Braves only really have Chris Sale and should win the first game. I just don't know if they will close out the series. I'd lean to them since they have home-field advantage and likely will take the opener. I really need to see how the Philadelphia rotation aligns before wagering on it.

I'm taking the Padres, and I'm taking over 2.5 games in this one. Simply put, the Cubs don't have the pitching staff to advance. Their starters have been rocked all year and continue to give up long ball after long ball. The offense has carried them, but as pitching gets tougher, it will be harder for them to score and be successful. Their defense could make a difference, but I just don't see it happening. The Padres have the better rotation, a lockdown closer, and have been playing great baseball over the past few months. I'm a Cubs fan, but I don't see it happening for them. Give me the Padres and a three-game series.

item.title: Trans NYT Games executive killed after accusing in-laws of years of abuse amid bitter custody battle
item.description: Jonathan McKinsey alleged years of abuse by his wife's parents in court filings before the Dublin, California, shooting that claimed his life Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
A transgender New York Times Games executive allegedly shot and killed by his wife's parents in Dublin, California, had accused them of years of abuse during a bitter custody and divorce battle, according to reports.

Jonathan McKinsey, 40, was fatally shot Saturday outside the Dublin Sports Grounds before police quickly arrested his parents-in-law, Shouyong Zhang, 77, and Shili Chen, 77, on suspicion of murder. Investigators have not said what led to the shooting.

The Mercury News, citing McKinsey's December 2025 petition for a domestic violence restraining order, reported that he alleged years of abuse by his estranged wife, Candice Jang, and her parents. The New York Times separately reported McKinsey, a transgender man, claimed the abuse stemmed from his gender identity.

IN-LAWS ARRESTED AFTER NEW YORK TIMES GAMES ENGINEERING DIRECTOR FOUND FATALLY SHOT

The newspapers reported McKinsey alleged Chen directed anti-LGBTQ slurs at him and one of the couple's children. He also claimed Jang mistreated him during medical procedures related to his gender transition and alleged his father-in-law hit him in the chest while he was recovering from double mastectomy surgery.

Fox News Digital reviewed court dockets showing McKinsey and Jang were involved in multiple legal proceedings at the time of his death, including competing domestic violence restraining order cases, an ongoing child custody dispute and a pending divorce.

WOMAN LINKED TO TRANSGENDER ZIZIAN CULT CHARGED WITH ARRANGING HER PARENTS' MURDERS ON HER 30TH BIRTHDAY

The dockets show Jang sought a domestic violence restraining order against McKinsey in October 2025, and McKinsey filed his own request two months later. The domestic violence matters were ultimately scheduled for a three-day hearing in December.

Separate court dockets show McKinsey faced a pending misdemeanor child abuse case filed in October 2025 charging him with child endangerment and corporal injury to a child. A pretrial hearing had been scheduled earlier this month.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

The Mercury News also reported Jang made competing allegations against McKinsey during the family court proceedings, accusing him of domestic violence and child abuse. McKinsey disputed those claims in his own petition, the newspaper reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Police have released few details about what led to Saturday's shooting, saying only that McKinsey was deliberately targeted.

SEND US A TIP

A Dublin Police Services sergeant driving near the sports complex spotted McKinsey lying in the parking lot shortly after 3 p.m. Saturday, prompting an immediate response from officers and paramedics.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

With help from witnesses, officers detained Zhang and Chen within minutes. Police said the married couple remained near the scene after the shooting.

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Both were booked into Santa Rita Jail on suspicion of murder. Jail records show prosecutors also recommended charges of conspiracy, willful discharge of a firearm and child abuse.

The investigation remains ongoing. Zhang and Chen are scheduled to be arraigned Wednesday morning in Alameda County.

It was not immediately clear if the defendants had attorneys representing them. Jang could not immediately be reached for comment.

item.title: Hollywood actress upset her son isn't gay fumes in bizarre spectacle at Human Rights Campaign gala
item.description: Camryn Manheim told the Human Rights Campaign dinner she "always wanted a gay son," but her boy turned out straight despite her very best efforts.
item.content:encoded:
A Hollywood actress used her platform on stage at a far-left Human Rights Campaign (HRC) event to complain that despite her best efforts, her son turned out to be heterosexual.

Camryn Manheim, best known for her role as Ellenor Frutt in the late 1990s and early 2000s drama series "The Practice," introduced and presented her friend and fellow actress Marcia Gay Harden with the Ally for Equality Award at the HRC's National Dinner on Sunday.

"For Marcia, of course, this is deeply personal to her," said Manheim of this year's recipient of the prestigious award. "She has three remarkable children who all align with the LGBTQ+ community, which is another thing that deeply irritates me about her, because I always wanted a gay son."

GLAAD RELEASES 'PARTICULARLY CONCERNING' REPORT SHOWING SHRINKING LGBTQ REPRESENTATION THIRD YEAR IN A ROW

She then launched into a tirade about how her son is heterosexual.

"I love that relationship between gay sons and their mothers," she said from the stage. "I wanted to be the picket sign-holding mom who would beat the s--- out of somebody for her kid. I mean, let's just admit it, gay sons are the best, right? Right!"

"I have photographs of my son in high heels, in full drag, he knows every word to every musical ever written, his fairy godfather, Aaron Walton, is here with us tonight. I mean, truly, I thought I had this f---ing thing locked up, but no, no, he's the only straight guy in his entire musical theater company," Manheim complained.

Manheim's only child, Milo Manheim, 25, is an actor best known for his starring role as Zed in the Disney Channel film franchise "Zombies." He played Joseph in the 2023 Christmas musical, "Journey to Bethlehem," and in 2018 came in second place on season 27 of "Dancing with the Stars."

LOG CABIN REPUBLICANS REMOVES 'T' FROM LGBT ADVOCACY, SAYS 'RADICAL' TRANS ACTIVISTS ARE ERODING GAY SUPPORT

Manheim, during her recorded remarks, relayed a story about Harden, a 2021 Oscar winner for best supporting actress in the 2000 film "Pollock," calling her a decade ago to tell her that her son was gay.

"All I said was, 'Oh my God, you are so f---ing lucky!" Manheim said, yelling into the microphone and drawing a round of applause from the crowd.

And about a week later, I was at Marcia's house for dinner when an Amazon package was delivered, and inside, I'm not kidding you, was a pair of thigh-high patent leather boots, like kinky boots," Manheim continued. "And I thought, 'oh come on, now she is just showing off!"

DEMOCRATS TURN ON CONGRESSIONAL HOPEFUL AFTER 'HIDING' LGBTQ+ VIEWS FROM MUSLIM VOTERS

HRC is America's largest civil rights group dedicated to "engaging and mobilizing millions of pro-equality voters and supporters to elect pro-equality leaders and to demand equity-based policies and legislation." The organization was founded in 1980 by gay rights lobbyist Steve Endean and today boasts 4 million members.

Sunday night's dinner was part of the Human Rights Campaign's events program, which it says reaches more than 20,000 people each year through 30 fundraising dinner events. It allows the group to "elevate LGBTQ+ candidates around the country, keep volunteers engaged, amplify our work in the local community, and solicit corporate sponsorships and donations through our auctions."

Online, reactions ranged from dismayed to disgusted.

"How do any straight males survive mothers like this? It's a miracle some of them come out normal," said a right-wing commentator who goes by Peachy Keenan.

"These people are mentally ill. They need to be institutionalized or thrown in prison for trying to groom children," said Andy Froemel.

"It’s the entertainment industry mothers who are the psychos," online personality @shipwreckedcrew, who boasts more than 180,000 followers, said.

"These people are sick," radio show host Joe Pagliarulo said.

"Liberalism is a performative sickness," said Jon Nanjarian.

Fox News Digital reached out to HRC and representatives for Manheim but did not hear back at time of publication.

item.title: Apple's $250M Siri settlement: How to claim up to $95
item.description: The $250 million Apple Siri AI settlement is now accepting claims, with eligible iPhone owners potentially receiving up to $95 per device.
item.content:encoded:
If you bought one of Apple's AI-ready iPhones because you expected the smarter Siri Apple had been talking about, check when you purchased it. You could have some money coming your way. A proposed $250 million Apple Siri settlement now has an open claims process for qualifying iPhone owners.

The case centers on allegations that consumers bought certain iPhones expecting Siri features powered by Apple Intelligence that they did not receive during the period covered by the lawsuit. Apple denies the allegations and says it did nothing improper or unlawful.

The amount may sound small next to the price of a new iPhone, but filing a claim could put as much as $95 per eligible device back in your pocket. There are a few important catches, though, including exactly which iPhone you bought and when you bought it.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways AI can help you get better healthcare.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT

The lawsuit is called Landsheft, et al. v. Apple Inc. and is pending in federal court in Northern California. The plaintiffs alleged that Apple promoted certain Siri features powered by Apple Intelligence, leading buyers to expect capabilities that were not delivered during the class period. Apple denies those allegations. The company agreed to put $250 million into a settlement fund rather than continue litigating the case. The agreement received preliminary court approval on July 17, 2026. The court has scheduled a final approval hearing for Feb. 24, 2027. That timing is especially interesting because Apple finally began rolling out its long-awaited Siri AI beta with iOS 27 in September 2026.

The updated Siri can use personal context from information on your device, handle follow-up questions and take more actions inside supported apps. We recently took a closer look at iOS 27 and the new Siri AI features.

The settlement covers seven models: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max. The regular iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus are excluded. Owning one of those eligible models alone does not qualify you. You must be the original purchaser and live in the United States. You also must have purchased the phone in the United States between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The purchase had to be for personal or business use rather than resale. There is another important requirement. When you submit the claim, you must confirm that you expected to receive certain Siri Apple Intelligence features when you bought the device and did not receive those features as expected. Businesses can qualify, too. The official settlement site has separate filing options for individuals and organizations that purchased eligible devices for business use.

The settlement sets the payment at $25 per eligible device, but the final amount can change. If fewer valid claims come in, the payment may increase to as much as $95 per eligible device. If more claims come in, the payment can fall below $25. Administrative costs, approved attorneys' fees and other court-approved expenses also come out of the $250 million fund. You can submit a claim for each eligible device you purchased. That could make the payout more meaningful for someone who bought multiple qualifying iPhones during the class period. However, nobody knows the final payment yet. The settlement administrator has to count and validate the claims before that figure can be determined.

12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW

The claims period officially opened on Sept. 21, 2026. You can file through the official Smartphone AI Settlement website at smartphoneaisettlement.com. The deadline is Dec. 21, 2026. The claim form asks for your contact information and information that can confirm your eligible purchase or ownership. You also need to certify that you expected the covered Siri Apple Intelligence features when you purchased your iPhone and did not receive them as expected. I would have your iPhone's serial number handy before you start. On your iPhone, open Settings, tap General, then tap About. Your serial number appears near the top of that screen. You can press and hold it to copy it. The settlement site also says you may find the serial number on the phone's original packaging or purchase documentation.

The official site says people who received an email or postcard can file a claim. It also says people who believe they belong to the settlement class can submit a valid claim even if they did not receive a notice. So, I would not automatically write this off because nothing showed up in your mailbox or inbox. Instead, compare your purchase with the eligibility requirements and use the official settlement site. Be careful with links arriving through unexpected texts or emails. Large settlements often attract phishing attempts because scammers know people are looking for claim information. I recommend going directly to the official settlement website rather than clicking a claim link in an unsolicited message.

Do not expect a payment right after submitting your claim. The court has scheduled its final approval hearing for Feb. 24, 2027. The judge will decide whether to give the settlement final approval. Appeals could delay the process further. The official settlement administrator says payments will be processed after the settlement becomes effective, assuming the court approves it and any appeals are resolved. In other words, filing now secures your claim before the deadline. The check or digital payment could come much later.

YOU COULD GET PAID FROM GOOGLE’S ANDROID DATA LAWSUIT

If you qualify but do nothing, you will not receive a settlement payment. You will also remain bound by the settlement if the court gives it final approval, which affects your ability to pursue your own case against Apple over the claims covered by this lawsuit. The deadline to request exclusion from the settlement or formally object is also Dec. 21, 2026. Anyone considering those options should read the official settlement notice carefully because the legal consequences differ from simply submitting a claim. CyberGuy reached out to Apple for additional comment but did not hear back before our deadline.

Apple spent a lot of time building excitement around what Apple Intelligence would bring to Siri. If you bought one of these iPhones expecting those promised features, you may have been left waiting much longer than expected. Apple has now agreed to put $250 million into a settlement fund while continuing to deny the allegations. If your iPhone and purchase date qualify, I would take a few minutes to check your eligibility and file a claim. You could receive as much as $95 per device, depending on how many valid claims come in. This is also a good reminder to pay close attention when a company promotes upcoming software features as part of the reason to buy new hardware. What you are promised at launch and what you can actually use on day one may be very different.

Did you buy an iPhone expecting Apple's new AI-powered Siri, and do you think a payment of up to $95 per device fairly reflects how long buyers had to wait? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Skydivers watch plane vanish from sight, make split-second decision to jump
item.description: Skydive Milwaukee jumpers spotted a single-engine plane vanish behind trees near East Troy, then leaped from their own aircraft to reach victims and try to help.
item.content:encoded:
A group of professional skydivers who witnessed a plane crash took an extraordinary route to the scene — jumping from their own aircraft to reach the victims.

The men, all experienced skydivers with Skydive Milwaukee, were preparing for a jump when they spotted a small plane near East Troy Municipal Airport on Sunday, according to the Town of East Troy Police Department.

John Bechtel, one of the skydivers, told local outlet WSMV the plane appeared to be flying unusually before disappearing behind a line of trees.

MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED

"He kind of banked up a little bit, and then, he disappeared behind the trees," Bechtel recalled.

"We were all sitting there waiting for him to show back up somewhere, and [he] never did," he added. "We all just kind of looked at each other like, ‘Did we just see a plane crash?’"

The single-engine plane had crashed in a cornfield near the airport.

The group quickly asked their pilot to identify a safe place for them to jump so that they could help.

PROBE UNDERWAY AS 7 FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SICKENED BY BAFFLING ODOR ON MAJOR AIRLINE

Air traffic control told the pilot it was his call whether to drop the skydivers over the area.

"It is your discretion if you want to drop jumpers over the area," air traffic control told the pilot, according to WSMV.

"Yes, I am going to drop a couple of them. Yeah, we are going to drop ‘em right now," the pilot reportedly replied.

The skydivers were the first to reach the crash site.

They alerted emergency crews.

One of the jumpers, a former paramedic, treated a person with a serious head injury until emergency service workers arrived.

All four people aboard the plane survived, with Bechtel saying that the timing "couldn’t have been any better."

"Had we left five minutes earlier, we wouldn’t have seen it," Bechtel told WSMV.

"Had we left 15 minutes later, we wouldn’t have been able to get there first and assist."

Bechtel said it was the first time he had ever jumped out of a plane to respond to an emergency situation.

"I’m just glad that we were able to do what we were able to do and get in and help," Bechtel said, per WSMV.

He added, "To be able to do this and to be able to help others in need — I would absolutely do that in a heartbeat."

item.title: Hero cop stopped synagogue massacre in Canada as Jewish group calls for armed guards
item.description: The Yom Kippur attack outside Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville has intensified demands for armed security at Jewish institutions across Canada.
item.content:encoded:
When a gunman approached a police cruiser outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, during Yom Kippur, approximately two dozen people were praying inside.

The armed officer sitting outside was not part of a permanent security system available to every synagogue in Canada. Police had dispatched him after receiving a report about a suspicious vehicle. That decision may have prevented a massacre. 

"The only thing that stood in the way of every congregant of that shul being murdered was the presence of an armed police officer," Simon Wolle, CEO of B’nai Brith Canada, told Fox News Digital.

ISRAELI MEDICS TRAIN US SYNAGOGUES HOW TO RESPOND TO ATTACKS, AS HIGH HOLIDAYS APPROACH

Police said last week's shooting was a deliberate, hate-motivated attack targeting the Jewish community. According to authorities, 29-year-old Sean Ward approached Belleville Police Constable Jeff Smith and allegedly shouted, "You are going to die for the Jews," before firing a shotgun at him.

Smith was struck multiple times while still inside his vehicle. Despite his injuries, he emerged from the cruiser and returned fire. A second officer arrived within minutes and joined the confrontation. Ward later died at a hospital.

Smith remains hospitalized after suffering multiple gunshot wounds to his head and body and serious head trauma. Belleville Police Chief Murray Rodd said Smith faces multiple surgeries and a "lengthy and challenging" recovery, but said the officer is "making progress every day."

Smith’s wife, Ashley, has also spoken publicly about her husband’s recovery, describing the shooting as "the scariest and darkest day of our lives."

"My words aren’t strong or steady yet, but I knew I needed to find them," she wrote. "I needed to use my voice for my dear Jeff, until he is able to use his."

MAN CHARGED WITH ASSAULT, HATE CRIMES AFTER ALLEGEDLY DISRUPTING SHABBAT SERVICES AT NYC SYNAGOGUE

Ashley Smith also addressed the Jewish community directly, thanking those who have supported her husband and their family. "Please know that your love, your prayers and your support have reached us," she wrote. "We are deeply grateful. We love you, we see you, we pray for you."

She said her husband still faces "a very long, difficult road ahead," but added that he is surrounded by what she called "an army of love."

The worshipers inside the synagogue were not physically injured.

Investigators later disclosed that the gunman possessed what Belleville Police Chief Murray Rodd described as the "means, motive and mechanisms to cause a mass casualty and the destruction of the Jewish synagogue." Police also reported discovering combustible materials inside the suspect’s vehicle.

"This individual had the means, the intention, the deliberate plans and the capacity to conduct a murderous massacre," Wolle said.

For Wolle, the attack exposed more than a violent act of antisemitism. It revealed a legal and security system that he believes leaves Canadian Jewish institutions dangerously vulnerable.

B’nai Brith Canada is calling for changes to federal and provincial laws that would allow synagogues, Jewish schools and other vulnerable institutions to hire qualified armed security guards.

"There is currently no legislation in place that allows for Jewish institutions to hire the kind of armed protection that may be necessary," Wolle said.

Canada’s firearms regulations are controlled at the federal level, while private security is also governed through separate provincial rules. Wolle said those frameworks must be aligned so institutions confronting credible threats have a lawful way to employ trained, licensed armed guards.

FLORIDA MAN INDICTED FOR ALLEGEDLY PLOTTING MASS SHOOTING TARGETING JEWISH EMPLOYEES AT ADVOCACY ORGANIZATION

At present, he said, Jewish institutions can ask police departments to increase patrols, although departments cannot always guarantee that an officer will be stationed outside. Communities can also try to hire paid-duty police officers, but availability remains limited.

"So the only option right now for the Jewish community to protect itself from the unprecedented amount of violent attacks taking place all across this country is to plead with local police services to come by if they can," Wolle said. "They will not guarantee that they will do so in most circumstances."

That leaves Jewish communities spending their own money to reinforce buildings, install surveillance systems and hire officers when available.

"Right now, the Jewish community is using its own money primarily to build walls, put up stronger fences, add cameras and then pay for the privilege of having an armed police officer," Wolle said. "Our lives are being threatened across the country, and the government hasn’t taken the steps to offer the necessary protection."

B’nai Brith has made two requests. It wants laws amended to permit qualified armed private security at vulnerable Jewish institutions, and it wants the government to fund an increased police presence at those locations.

Wolle said the burden of protecting Jewish Canadians from targeted violence should not rest solely on the people being threatened.

"The government needs to meet its most basic obligation and responsibility, which is to protect its citizens," he said.

The numbers provide a stark context for his concerns. Statistics Canada recorded 788 police-reported hate crimes targeting Jewish people in 2025, representing more than 70% of all reported religiously motivated hate crimes that year.

Wolle said Jewish Canadians constitute approximately 1% to 2% of the country’s population, yet remain overwhelmingly affected by religiously motivated hate crimes. Preliminary data from B’nai Brith’s 2026 annual audit indicate that violent antisemitic incidents have already more than tripled compared with the total recorded throughout 2025.

"There is a national crisis of Jew hatred in Canada," Wolle said.

B’nai Brith has been warning for months that antisemitic violence is accelerating. Wolle said the organization submitted recommendations and concrete plans to different levels of government before the Belleville attack.

"We’ve been calling for many things from all levels of government," he said. "We provided concrete action plans to each."

The shooting has intensified the organization’s demand that lawmakers treat the security of Jewish institutions as an emergency rather than another subject for future discussion.

"The most urgent thing that is needed is a mechanism for there to be armed protection of Jewish institutions that are under attack right now in Canada," Wolle said.

He emphasized that B’nai Brith is not calling for firearms to be placed indiscriminately inside synagogues and schools. Its proposal concerns trained, vetted and qualified security professionals operating under a clearly defined legal framework.

"If we don’t have enough armed officers, then we need legislative frameworks changed to allow for alternative armed guards to protect Jewish institutions," Wolle said.

Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the Belleville attack and called on anyone with information to contact law enforcement.

RECORD ANTISEMITIC INCIDENTS IN CANADA FUEL CRITICISM OF CARNEY GOVERNMENT RESPONSE

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

"On the holiest night of the Jewish calendar, a shooting took place outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville," Carney said. "Jewish people must be able to worship safely. To live free, open, proud Jewish lives."

Wolle welcomes expressions of support and said Canadian Jews now need their government to move beyond statements.

"The government gives us words and no action," he added.

Belleville offered a disturbing picture of what could have happened without an armed officer outside. The congregants did not know that a man police say was driven by hatred had allegedly arrived with weapons and the capacity to cause mass casualties.

One report of a suspicious vehicle led to one officer being placed outside. That officer, Wolle stressed, became the barrier between the gunman and the people praying inside.

"In the wake of these harrowing events, Canada’s Jewish community cannot wait any longer for the government to act," he said.

The people inside the synagogue, Sons of Jacob, survived. Wolle’s warning is that Canada cannot depend on chance, a suspicious-vehicle report or the availability of a single officer the next time a Jewish institution is targeted.

"This is not a Jewish community problem," he said. "This is a Canadian problem."

item.title: Forgotten coffee brands Americans grew up with — and what happened to them
item.description: Starbucks and Dunkin' Donuts reshaped coffee culture, but brands like Gold Shield and Savarin still stir powerful nostalgia this National Coffee Day.
item.content:encoded:
Long before Starbucks became shorthand for coffee culture, Americans were opening cans of coffee from brands like Gold Shield, Savarin and Schilling. This National Coffee Day, many of those once-familiar names exist mostly in memory.

But that may be exactly why they still resonate.

"I think there's a lot of nostalgia and romance around coffee because I do think it's such an important part of daily life," said Wendy Pojmann, a professor of history at Siena University who has studied coffee culture and wrote "Espresso: The Art and Soul of Italy."

6 ICONIC AMERICAN RESTAURANTS STILL SERVING UP NOSTALGIA AND CLASSIC FLAVORS

For people who grew up with those brands, Pojmann said the connection often goes beyond what was in the cup.

"So, I do think that, especially if you grew up and you smelled the coffee in the kitchen and maybe your mom and dad or your grandparents were preparing a certain kind of coffee, those memories are important, and we associate memory with smell," she told Fox News Digital.

Coffee culture looked different then, too. Convenience helped define the American coffee routine, from instant coffee to the automatic drip machines that became fixtures in American kitchens.

"Americans, again, were interested in ease, efficiency, things being relatively quick," Pojmann said, describing a routine that might include grabbing a big can of Folgers from the grocery store and brewing it at home.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Folgers and Maxwell House endured, but plenty of other familiar names did not. Smaller regional and local coffee brands were often acquired by larger companies, Pojmann said, part of a cycle of consolidation that has played out repeatedly in the coffee business.

Gold Shield, a once-popular West Coast brand, and Savarin, a longtime East Coast favorite, were among the coffee labels that eventually disappeared after changing hands.

Their fate reflected a broader consolidation in the coffee business, as larger companies acquired smaller regional and local brands, Pojmann said.

Then came another shift. Chains such as Starbucks and Dunkin' helped reshape American coffee culture, followed by the rise of specialty coffee and a new generation of small roasters and boutique brands.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

More recently, specialty coffee has created another generation of small roasters and boutique brands.

Pojmann said today's coffee market includes everything from huge national brands to tiny small-batch roasters.

Still, a coffee brand doesn't necessarily disappear when its cans leave supermarket shelves.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Pojmann said she sometimes spots tins from bygone brands in vintage and antique stores, where an old label can unexpectedly reconnect someone with the past.

"Maybe you hadn't thought of it in years and then you see that label on the can and you think, 'Oh yeah, I remembered my grandfather used to make that coffee for us,'" Pojmann said.

For some coffee drinkers, a favorite old brand may be long gone from the supermarket aisle. But the smell of a pot brewing can still bring back memories of the people who once poured it.

item.title: Iowa wide receiver 'blacked out' after hauling in last-second game winner against Michigan
item.description: Reece Vander Zee says he "blacked out" during his game-winning catch as time expired, revealing the Hawkeyes practice that exact play weekly.
item.content:encoded:
Iowa wide receiver Reece Vander Zee hauled in the catch of a lifetime as time expired in The Big House, but don't ask him to recount what exactly went down on the field.

Vander Zee, who led the Hawkeyes in receptions against Michigan in Week 4, caught a 16-yard pass from quarterback Hank Brown to hand the Hawkeyes a stunning 20-19 win on the road against the Wolverines.

It was one of those magical moments, at least if you're an Iowa fan, that portrays the magic of college football, and while Vander Zee explained that the Hawkeyes routinely run that exact play during practice, he doesn't remember any of the exact details about the game-winner.

FLORIDA GATORS, MISSISSIPPI STATE SOAR, USC TUMBLES IN LATEST INEXPLICABLE AP TOP 25 POLL

"We run that play every week, just you know, end of game situations, we do that every week," the junior pass catcher explained on Sirius XM. "It was crazy, I kind of blacked out. Don’t really remember. I just remember all my teammates in my face. But yeah, it was just a great great team win. It’s just great to see everybody having a good time. You know, coach Ferentz is just as happy as anyone, and just great to be great to play for him and great to have this opportunity, so it’s awesome."

While the throw and catch between Brown and Vander Zee as time expired will go down in Iowa history, so too will the final drive the Hawkeyes put together to pull off the stunner.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Trailing by five, Iowa received the ball with 1:37 remaining in the game before using its final timeout with 34 seconds on the clock on its own 42-yard line. A 15-yard penalty on Michigan with 26 seconds left moved the ball into Michigan territory, but the Hawkeyes didn't move the football again until a 29-yard completion with two ticks on the clock.

Michigan defender John Henry Daley went down with an injury, which stopped the clock in a situation where Iowa may not have gotten another play off, but when gifted a stoppage in play, the Hawkeyes delivered the goods with a perfect ball from Brown into the hands of Vander Zee.

Iowa moved to 4-0 on the year, setting up a massive showdown this Saturday against 3-1 Ohio State, while the Wolverines dropped to 3-1 and lost a huge margin for error if they want to make the College Football Playoff.

item.title: Republicans fear they ‘haven’t done a damn thing’ to lower prices ahead of midterm reckoning
item.description: Senate Republicans spent weeks passing the Protect College Sports Act while Sen. Josh Hawley and others warn affordability concerns are being ignored.
item.content:encoded:
The key focus of this election, like many before it, is the economy, but the Senate has spent its waning weeks in Washington focusing on something else: college sports.

And that has proven a sticking point for some Republicans who are eager to maintain power in the upper chamber and worried that they aren’t meeting the moment to address voters’ concerns over the cost-of-living.

"I'm just hoping that this will be the best bill ever passed by the United States Senate considering the ungodly amount of time we've spent on it," Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told Fox News Digital.

"So maybe this will be the most perfect and pristine piece of legislation ever," he quipped.

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

"There's a lot of things we could be doing and should be doing," the senator added. "So I hope we'll do those before we leave. We'll see."

Hawley rattled off those issues that he hoped lawmakers would tackle that all ended in one word, costs — be it for fuel, prescription drugs, health care or the financial burden of the artificial intelligence boom.

The Senate is expected to leave the nation’s capital on Wednesday to hit the campaign trail for the homestretch of the fast-approaching midterm elections. But from the summer of 2025 to now, with several shutdowns and partisan fights in between, the sting on voters’ wallets, to some concerned Republicans, has become an afterthought.

Still, Republicans are quick to tout their accomplishments from last year, notably the "big, beautiful bill," as their signature achievement to tackle the growing issue of affordability in the country — it was a predominant pitch during the midterm convention in Dallas earlier this month, and can be heard increasingly in the halls of the Senate as Nov. 3 nears.

SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS

The concern over inaction in the recent weeks and months has intensified as the main business in the Senate has been devoted to passing the Protect College Sports Act from Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, which cruised through the upper chamber late Monday night.

"We've been spending all week on trying to make the football coaches happy," Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said. "I'm voting for the bill, but I can assure that moms and dads out there across America, when they lie down to sleep at night … they're not worried about the football coaches."

Kennedy said that he and others have been pressuring Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., to take another shot at reconciliation tailored exclusively toward affordability issues, or at the very least to put a bill that would shield consumers from increasing electricity costs as part of the AI boom.

"Because we haven't done a damn thing," Kennedy said. "And it's biting us in the ass right now."

ANXIETY GROWS OVER EMERGING ELECTION ISSUE, BUT GOP SAYS WASHINGTON ISN'T THE ANSWER

Thune did tee up what will likely be the Senate’s last attempt at dealing with affordability for a vote this week on a bill that would require AI companies to bear the brunt of rising utility costs from data centers.

That bill, from Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is expected to be blocked by Democrats, however, who aren’t eager to give Republicans or Trump a victory — especially so close to the midterm elections.

But for some Republicans, it’s too little too late when it comes to actually trying to address voters’ worries.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., recalled a story when he won the North Carolina House and became speaker. He ran to fix the economy, and once he won the power to do so, he and Republicans in the state would have to own the issue, regardless of the previous administration’s actions.

"That's how you actually show some leadership and get it done. You can't rationalize that we're here because of a problem caused by the prior administration," Tillis told Fox News Digital. "That's how we got elected. But you gotta fix it if you promise to. And that's what we have to work on. I just think rationalizing away, that's just not good politics."

Still, Republicans are asking for a second chance this fall, specifically Vice President JD Vance, who earlier this month asked voters to "give us another chance."

When asked about Vance’s plea, Tillis said, "You know what? If it works, it'll be a first."

item.title: FBI strikes back at hacking group with overseas arrest of alleged leader
item.description: A 24-year-old Amsterdam man was arrested by Dutch police and the FBI for allegedly leading the ShinyHunters global hacking syndicate network.
item.content:encoded:
An alleged leader of the notorious global hacking syndicate ShinyHunters has been arrested in the Netherlands following a joint operation between the FBI and Dutch authorities, targeting a cybercrime network linked to high-profile attacks across the U.S. and worldwide.

Dutch police announced the arrest of a 24-year-old Amsterdam man Sept. 15 for his alleged role in the ShinyHunters hacking group and for attempting to incite two murders, with authorities noting that further arrests remain possible as they investigate seized electronic devices.

"This morning @FBI and our partners the Dutch National Police are announcing the arrest of one of the alleged leaders of ShinyHunters – a global cybercrime and threat actor group linked to cyberattacks in the United States, the Netherlands, and around the world," FBI Director Kash Patel wrote Tuesday morning on X. 

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

"In coordination with FBI investigators the Dutch High-Tech Crime Unit arrested the suspect under Dutch law. As we speak FBI teams are actively working with partners to obtain and execute more leads in the ongoing investigation based on this arrest. 

"Thank you to our Dutch National Police partners for their continued work with us in this case and the industry partners who shared information with us. The investigation continues."

"The man is also suspected of attempted incitement to commit two murders," according to a Dutch police release. "Various data carriers have been seized and are being investigated further. Further arrests are not ruled out."

Brett Leatherman, assistant director of ​the FBI's ⁠Cyber Division, made an unusually public address to the hacking group ShinyHunters, telling the cybercriminals that "we know how to find you." 

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

"You know how to find us, and we know how to find you," Leatherman said in a video statement. "I suggest you reach out first while the choice is still yours."

Benjamin Korper of Amsterdam-based cybersecurity company Neo Security named the arrested man as Pepijn van der Stap, the company's offensive security lead.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Korper said Dutch forensic investigators visited his office Sept. 15, the night Van der Stap was arrested in a dramatic police raid that involved flash bang grenades.

ShinyHunters is a hacking group known for large-scale data breaches and extortion and had announced its recent theft of what it said was terabytes of sensitive personnel data from U.S. FBI servers, including intelligence assignments and medical records of employees, according to Reuters.

FBI EXTRADITES CHINESE HACKER ACCUSED OF STEALING COVID-19 RESEARCH

An internal memo circulated to staffers said the FBI was operating under the presumption that hackers stole data pertaining to all bureau employees, a source told Reuters.

In a statement, ShinyHunters said Van der Stap had "no association" with the group and that Dutch police were incompetent. 

News of Van der Stap's arrest caused a stir in the cybersecurity community.

Van der Stap's 2023 convictions of data theft and extortion had already received widespread publicity, as did his subsequent public disavowal of cybercrime. On his personal website, Van der Stap acknowledged his journey "hasn't been a straight line" but said his experience had taught him that "knowledge is for building and protecting, not breaking."

FBI SAYS SOURCE OF ITS JOBS PORTAL BREACH STILL UNKNOWN AS HACKERS ALLEGE EMPLOYEE DATA COMPROMISED

Korper said he had carefully vetted Van der Stap before hiring him, monitored him during his employment, and was shocked by the arrest.

"I truly believe that people deserve a second chance, but in this case I was not thanked for it," Korper said. "Absolutely everybody I talked to is flabbergasted."

The executive said he had hired an outside firm to investigate whether Van der Stap had hacked Neo Security or its customers, but so far investigators have found no evidence that he acted against his employer or its clients.

Korper and Van der Stap have not been in touch since the arrest, Korper said.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Inside Operation Blackout: Patel reveals global scam ‘cities’ targeting your parents’ life savings
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel says Operation Blackout has seized roughly $17 billion tied to scam compounds targeting senior citizens across the globe.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: FBI Director Kash Patel says the bureau is expanding its global hunt for sprawling scam compounds that prey heavily on Americans, telling Fox News Digital that Operation Blackout has seized roughly $17 billion tied to the schemes. 

"At 71 years old, I'm old enough to know that people my age are certainly often targeted because of our unfamiliarity with certain new technologies. Thanks so much for looking out for us," one victim told the FBI.

"I watched my grandmother lose her life savings to scammers and I would love to see them all be put away," said another victim.

Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global campaign to identify, disrupt and dismantle foreign scam compounds targeting Americans, combining overseas raids and asset seizures with efforts to cut off the networks’ communications, rescue trafficked workers and return stolen money to victims.

FBI WRAPS UP CYBERCRIME OPERATION TARGETING GLOBAL NETWORKS PREYING ON AMERICANS

Patel said the FBI-led initiative is targeting criminal syndicates operating massive scam compounds across Southeast Asia and the Middle East, where trafficked workers are forced to carry out fraud schemes against victims thousands of miles away.

"Unfortunately, the majority of the targets are senior citizens in America," Patel told Fox News, pointing to schemes carried out through social media, phone calls, text messages and Telegram.

FBI SEIZES RECORD-SETTING $8 BILLION IN CRYPTOCURRENCY AMID INTERCONTINENTAL 'SCAM COMPOUND' CRACKDOWN

In one common version of the scheme, criminals cultivate an online friendship or relationship with a victim before steering them toward a fraudulent cryptocurrency investment platform.

Victims may initially believe their investments are generating significant returns, only to discover they cannot withdraw their money.

"These are towns, these are cities," Patel said of the scam compounds targeted by the operation. "These are actual villages with structures where they force people into forced labor."

An August operation at Cambodia’s roughly 200-acre O’Smach Resort scam compound involved searches of 28 buildings over three days and resulted in the seizure of 113 hard drives, 15 computers and 35 boxes of evidence, according to the FBI.

The bureau is also trying to stop Americans from becoming victims before their money ever reaches the scammers.

SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO

Under Operation Level Up, its domestic prevention component, the FBI proactively identifies and contacts potential victims of cryptocurrency investment scams. The bureau says it has notified 10,406 victims and prevented an estimated $660 million in losses, while seizing or freezing another $122 million in cryptocurrency.

The FBI said 77% of the people it contacted did not know they were being scammed. The bureau has also referred 99 victims for suicide intervention, seized 584 scam websites and sent 7,670 scam accounts to private-sector companies for action.

THE SECRET LIST THAT TELLS SCAMMERS YOU'RE AN EASY TARGET

In September, a DOJ Scam Center Strike Force team that included FBI Honolulu personnel helped authorities in Madagascar take down 13 scam centers operated by Chinese organized crime syndicates and process more than 3,200 electronic devices.

Patel said the geographic shift is part of a broader migration by the criminal networks.

"That’s why you’re seeing the migration of these scam compounds to central and sub-Saharan Africa, which is where we are already pre-positioned to take them off," Patel said.

item.title: I've battled gangs for decades. Now I'm fighting a threat that's even harder
item.description: Drill rap livestreams on smartphones are leading to shootings and funerals on Chicago's South Side, where location tags become deadly dares.
item.content:encoded:
In my time on the South Side of Chicago, I’ve asked people to look at what we’re losing. I have pointed out the root causes of gun violence, set up programs to counter it, confronted gangsters and brought them to truces, and helped many enter mainstream society as productive citizens. I’ve created after-school programs to counter our failing public schools so that kids won’t give up on themselves. But lately, I’ve been looking at another problem that may just be equally dangerous: the smartphone.

When you look at a smartphone, it doesn’t look like a threat. It looks like a tool for connection and even for opportunity. And for a lot of young people in my neighborhood, it has been exactly that — a way to make music, create an online following and learn about worlds outside of this block. I don’t want to discount what they have done because some have built real careers with nothing but a phone and its many tools. That’s a genuine way out of poverty, and I have no desire to shut that door.

But I can’t ignore the dark side of the phone.

AMERICA MOCKED THE AMISH AND OTHER GROUPS OVER TECHNOLOGY. MAYBE THEY WERE RIGHT

What I feel is that far too few of us acknowledge the full power of the phone. I once watched a documentary that said the power of all the computers needed to put the first man on the moon now existed in our tiny little phones. I don’t know if that’s true, but there is no doubt about the phone’s power. It puts the entire world at a kid’s fingertips.

Where I’ve seen the most devastating impact of the smartphone is in the world of drill rap, which began on O-Block, where my church and community center sit. Drill rap means "kill rap." Some of it is honest storytelling about a life that most of the country has never seen. But some of it has become a weapon. 

Fights that we used to see on corners have now moved onto livestreams. What happens is that a location tag is then dropped. Sometimes it’s dropped when a drill rap crew chooses to film in the wrong neighborhood as a dare. This dropping of a location is not an accident but a challenge: Come and get us. 

INDIANA REPUBLICAN SENATOR MOVES TO BLOCK KIDS FROM ACCESSING PORN ONLINE

So we have kids watching these livestreams, half listening to the rap and half waiting for that burst of gunfire to come. When the latter happens, it is me or one of the nearby pastors who has to host the funeral. We then have to send our violence impact teams to the hospitals and homes of families to prevent retaliatory shootings. All from a livestream playing out on the phones of 10-, 12-, 14- and 17-year-olds.

So the same phone that can build a young artist up — and, man, some of these kids are so talented — that same phone can bring them down. When there is a shooting, the police and prosecutors comb through all these livestreams, and any comments may be treated as confessions. Whatever you think of this legal strategy, some of these kids get locked up.

But the phone isn’t only a problem on the streets. Parents here struggle with the problem of the phone in their homes. I see this in good families that are far removed from the life of gangs or drill rap. Their kids simply cannot put the phone down. Kids can access pornography even before they’ve had a chance to form healthy relationships. Our communities don’t teach courtship much anymore, and for the last several decades, we’ve lived in this hookup culture. So what does a child wired by pornography think when he or she encounters the other sex?

Parents often tell me the same thing, and I’m struck by how similar the wording is. It goes something like this: "I don’t know how to take the phone away from my child. It’s like I’m ending their world. I don’t know if I even have the authority to do it. They tell me that if I do, I’m cutting them off. It just becomes an endless battle."

WHAT META'S NEW TEEN RESTRICTIONS MEAN FOR YOUNG PEOPLE

The reality is that the phone often turns into a weapon that the child uses against the authority of the parent. I’ve heard kids tell their parents that they are smarter than them. That’s nothing but an illusion. When a child Googles or uses AI while arguing against a parent, that’s not the same thing as learning or processing the actual argument. That’s using a machine to speak for oneself. And what this ultimately does is stop the child from respecting the authority and knowledge of the parent. 

Parents are not always right, but the phone deprives the child and parent of the process of working through that misunderstanding and, in turn, weakens the fabric of their relationship.

That’s the real crisis. Not the technology itself — the erosion of the adult’s ability to set a limit on it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The solution is not a ban. What I’m calling for is a shift in the culture. We need to return to the basic authority that parents used to take for granted. Yes, take that phone away at night. Yes, put limits on the phone. Yes, tell your child to sit at the table and do homework. Go to church. Look people in the eye when talking. Make them look at reality instead of a screen.

And one thing that we need to do is support these parents. We adults who make up this community must echo this pushback against the phone, so the kids understand that it is not just their parents but the entire community pushing back.

We have fought many problems in my community, from drugs to gangs. The phone may be even harder. But I’ll leave you with this thought: A phone cannot love a child. It can only hold their eyes through the trickery of the algorithm. But somebody has to be there to hold that child and to love that child, and that must be us.

item.title: Video shows Florida food truck workers fleeing from ICE during Tallahassee immigration raid
item.description: Video captures food truck workers scrambling as ICE federal agents arrive at a Tallahassee Florida, taqueria, with one woman seen being apprehended.
item.content:encoded:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raid in Tallahassee, Florida, prompted mass chaos as security footage showed food truck workers scrambling to flee from federal agents on Friday.

Workers at Chile & Chili’s Taqueria Tallahassee scurried in and out of the food truck’s trailers when federal authorities rolled onto the scene, according to video obtained by Fox News Digital.

Video shows one of the workers, a woman, being apprehended by authorities.

item.title: Mamdani deflects Kimmel's anti-Trump bait when pressed repeatedly on relationship with the president
item.description: Zohran Mamdani dodged Jimmy Kimmel's attempts to get him to bash President Donald Trump in several questions asked about the nature of their relationship.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani seemed to deflect late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's questions about his relationship with President Donald Trump, as the mayor avoided bashing him and rejected the late-night host's request to send him a selfie.

"Did you guys hit it off immediately or is it something that you really went into thinking, like, ‘OK, I need to have a relationship with the president of the United States and I think the best way to do it is to charm him?' How did you do that and can you help me?" Kimmel asked Mamdani, calling his relationship with Trump "unexpected."

Mamdani responded, "Sorry, brother."

The mayor told Kimmel he and the president had many disagreements, but agreed on how much they both love New York City.

MAMDANI DESCRIBES TRUMP RELATIONSHIP AS 'HONEST' AND 'DIRECT' AMID RECENT BLOWOUT

"And so, from that first meeting in November of last year, I was just thinking of, ‘How can we make this meeting not about us, but about New Yorkers? How can we spend that time talking about the things that could make life in the city that little bit easier?’ And that's what it's been whether we've met at the White House or at Gracie Mansion," he said.

Mamdani and the president met earlier this month at the mayor's residence, Gracie Mansion, despite the major policy differences the two have.

"The number one thing that we've been speaking about recently has been Sunnyside Yard, which is this idea for decades of building a platform over a rail yard and then building 12,000 homes. And so, in that moment, you know, that you zoomed in on, I'm just thinking about 12,000 homes, 30,000 jobs, largest housing development since the early 1970s," Mamdani told Kimmel.

TRUMP'S HOUSING CHIEF PAINTS A GRIM PICTURE FOR HOMEOWNERSHIP IN ONE MAJOR AMERICAN CITY

Kimmel asked, "When you text him about Sunnyside, are you sure he doesn't think you're texting him about eggs?"

Mamdani said he was "pretty sure" and noted that the texts were pretty normal and didn't resemble the president's Truth Social posts.

"Wow. You really have broken through with him," Kimmel said. "I mean listen, you seem to be doing a great job in New York.We might need you to move to Washington just hang out at the Oval Office all day. Like if you texted him a selfie of us right now."

Mamdani laughed and shut it down.

"I love you, but I love housing more," Mamdani responded.

Kimmel went on to ask if Mamdani would come be the mayor of Los Angeles at the end of the discussion.

MAMDANI, LETITIA JAMES SUE TO BLOCK TRUMP ADMIN FROM REFUSING IMMIGRANTS OVER WELFARE STATUS

The White House did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Trump first met with the socialist mayor last November and said Mamdani could "surprise some conservative people" and declared, "The better he does, the happier I am."

Their last meeting, on Feb. 26 at the Oval Office, was notably cordial, with Mamdani seeking Trump’s support for an ambitious New York housing proposal despite their political differences.

"The new communist mayor of New York City, I think he’s a nice guy, actually," Trump said in his State of the Union address in February. "I speak to him a lot. Bad policy, but nice guy."

item.title: Rahm Emanuel expresses support for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador Rahm Emanuel insisted the DSA are a separate party, yet he backed Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
AUSTIN, TEXAS — Former U.S. ambassador and lifelong Democrat Rahm Emanuel doubled down on his declaration that democratic socialists don't belong in his party while expressing support for a far-left candidate competing in one of the most highly contested Senate races in the midterms.

"Democratic Socialists are a separate party. I'll see you in November," Emanuel told Fox News Digital at the Texas Tribune Festival.

Emanuel, who has been mulling a 2028 presidential bid, has been outspoken against the far-left. While he insisted that the Democratic Socialists of America are their own party, they've made their mark on the Democratic ballot, particularly in the 2026 midterms.

Democratic socialists have won several congressional Democratic primaries across the country, including three candidates in New York City who were endorsed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, as well as Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania, Melat Kiros in Colorado and Florida Senate hopeful Angie Dixon.

RAHM EMANUEL TOUTS WHAT SEPARATES HIMSELF FROM OTHER DEMS AS HE MULLS 2028 PRESIDENTIAL BID

Despite the major gains this election cycle, Emanuel insisted there's no "takeover" of his party.

"You think people wanna support defunding the police? You think they wanna support open borders, open prisons? Run on it. I don't, and that's not the party's position," Emanuel said. "Now, we will have healthy debate among progressive and pragmatic wing of the party. That's what a coalition party looks like. But that is it. You had a party convention!"

"Swing voters in swing states swing presidential elections. That is it. It's not more complicated. And you better be focused on winning," he added.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS DSA AGENDA DOESN'T PLAY WELL OUTSIDE 'UPPER WEST SIDE OF MANHATTAN'

Prominent Democratic Socialists like Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., have rallied behind Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, though El-Sayed claims not to be a socialist himself.

While speaking at the Texas Tribune Festival, Emanuel didn't hesitate to praise Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico, calling him "strong" and admiring Talarico for being "comfortable" about discussing his faith. 

But when asked by Fox News Digital moments later whether he supports El-Sayed's candidacy, Emanuel initially hedged.

RAHM EMANUEL WARNS ‘BERNIE BROS’ COULD SINK DEMOCRATS BY SADDLING MODERATES WITH SOCIALIST AGENDA

"Look, I mean, it doesn't matter what I do ... it matters what the Michigan voters think," he told Fox News Digital. "And that's what's gonna determine this in this effort. And I support the Democrats winning the Senate."

"So, in effect, you do hope that he wins that race for Democrats," Fox News Digital followed.

"Yeah," Emanuel answered.

Fox News Digital's Brian Flood contributed to this report.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Hegseth to double cuts to generals, admirals in major Pentagon shakeup
item.description: Pete Hegseth's State of the Force address doubles last year's cuts, targeting a 20% reduction in general and flag officer billets across all services.
item.content:encoded:
War Secretary Pete Hegseth will announce plans to reduce by 20% the number of positions reserved for generals and admirals during his State of the Force address on Wednesday.

Hegseth approved reduction plans for the Army, Navy, Air Force and the military's joint pool earlier this month, according to memos seen by Fox News Digital. The services were directed to implement the plans and complete the reductions by Jan. 1, 2027.

Wednesday's address in Quantico, Va. is expected to lay out Hegseth's priorities for the military in the year ahead, with the reduction in senior leadership positions among the changes he will unveil.

The new target doubles the 10% overall reduction in general and flag officer positions Hegseth ordered last year as part of his effort to streamline the military's senior ranks. That earlier directive separately called for a 20% reduction in active-duty four-star positions and a 20% reduction in National Guard general officers.

SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES

Hegseth dubbed that effort "less generals, more GIs," arguing that reducing senior headquarters positions would push resources and authority toward troops closer to the fight.

The latest reductions apply to billets — positions designated for generals and admirals — rather than an across-the-board removal of 20% of the officers currently serving in those ranks, a War Department source told Fox News Digital.

At least some of the positions will be downgraded rather than eliminated altogether. In a Sept. 16 memo approving reductions to the military's joint pool, Hegseth directed officials to establish O-6 requirements for general and flag officer positions identified for downgrade, allowing colonels and Navy captains to fill those jobs.

GOP REP THOMAS MASSIE INTRODUCES 8 ARTICLES OF IMPEACHMENT AGAINST WAR SECRETARY PETE HEGSETH

The announcement comes exactly one year after Hegseth summoned hundreds of generals and admirals from around the world to Quantico, Virginia, for an extraordinary gathering where he laid out his expectations for the military's senior leaders and warned those who did not support his reforms to step aside.

Hegseth has argued that reducing the number of generals and admirals would strip away unnecessary layers of bureaucracy and push authority down the chain of command.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"This is not a slash-and-burn exercise meant to punish high-ranking officers," Hegseth said when he announced the earlier reductions in May 2025. "This has been a deliberative process, working with the Joint Chiefs of Staff with one goal: maximizing strategic readiness and operational effectiveness by making prudent reductions in the general and flag officer ranks."

This year's audience will look different. Military commands have been asked to send top-performing service members who meet fitness and body-composition requirements and maintain "impeccable" grooming and uniform standards, according to published reports on internal Pentagon guidance for the event. Some troops selected to attend are also expected to participate in a workout with Hegseth.

item.title: Nikole Hannah-Jones' daughter asks why her education was sacrificed for ideology, says 'it makes no sense'
item.description: Nikole Hannah-Jones and her daughter Najya clashed on a podcast over the 1619 Project founder's decision to send her to a majority-Black public school.
item.content:encoded:
New York Times journalist and 1619 Project founder Nikole Hannah-Jones and her daughter Najya revisited their disagreement over Hannah-Jones' decision to send Najya to predominantly Black public schools, a choice Hannah-Jones now says she regrets aspects of, in a recent episode of "This American Life."

Both Hannah-Jones and her 16-year-old daughter appeared on the podcast, where Najya expressed her thoughts about her mother's viral New York Times Magazine essay, in which Hannah-Jones revisited her decision to choose her daughter's school in an effort to challenge school segregation.

Though Najya told the podcast that she had never read her mother's original essay, she called out her mother's reasoning for sending her to what she considered a lesser-quality school.

KAROL MARKOWICZ: 1619 PROJECT FOUNDER NIKOLE HANNAH-JONES LEARNED THE HARD TRUTH ABOUT SCHOOLS

"I didn't ever agree with her response," Najya said. "All I know is that I wasn't having it. I was just like, ‘why? Why am I here?’"

Najya was later allowed to choose her own high school, which was majority White and Asian. While she described the students as "too bougie" with "high egos," she struggled academically at first, and her parents arranged tutoring and other support as she caught up with her classmates.

During the podcast, Hannah-Jones and her daughter revisited their argument as Najya questioned why her education had to be sacrificed because other Black children were suffering.

"What do we then do? Do we just say, well, there's nothing I can do? Or do you try in some way to make some intervention? It's like, why should my child be the one that's rescued? You should escape what we consign so many other kids just like you to. I just will never feel right about that," Hannah-Jones said.

'THE VIEW' HOST SUNNY HOSTIN CLAIMS HER CHILDREN EXPERIENCED RACISM AT PRIVATE SCHOOLS

"Why? It makes no sense. You're talking about, 'Oh, I'm just going to give you the worst just because it's not fair that you' ... I didn't ask to be born. All you're supposed to do is just put me in a good school. Like, 'oh, well, I didn't want to put you in a great school and have you have advantages over other kids.' Isn't that what you want? Isn't that what you want me to have? Is that not a normal thing you want me to have?" Najya responded.

Najya also told Hannah-Jones that "everyone's not your kid" and that she "can't save everyone who doesn't want to be saved." She denied there were any benefits either to her or the school for being sent there.

"I wanted better. All the kids in my school that wanted better, wanted better. There's no benefit that came out of you putting me in those schools. There's no benefit at all. Could you tell me a benefit?" Najya said.

In Hannah-Jones' essay, she apologized to her daughter for her decision, writing that she felt Najya had been cheated educationally.

"Now I felt overcome with regret. Najya deserved better," Hannah-Jones wrote. "They all did. But she was mine. This girl, my only child, looked to me to protect her, to give her what she needed to thrive. And I had not chosen her."

Fox News Digital reached out to Hannah-Jones for comment.

OAKLAND SCHOOL DISTRICT VOWED REPARATIONS FOR BLACK STUDENTS, YET OUTCOMES APPEAR STAGNANT AFTER 5 YEARS

Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation and longtime school choice advocate, previously responded to Hannah-Jones' essay in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing parents should prioritize their children's individual educational needs.

"Parents should put their children first. They should not sacrifice them to a failing government school system in the name of ideology," DeAngelis said. "Nikole Hannah-Jones now says she regrets putting her ideals ahead of her daughter’s education. That admission is long overdue."

Hannah-Jones originally told Fox News Digital on Sunday after her essay was published that the broader focus should remain on families who lack the resources to pursue better educational options for their children.

"I hope people concerned about the choice my husband and I made for our daughter will have equal or more outrage for the thousands of Black children whose parents don’t have the resources to send them to better schools," she said. "As I write in the piece, there is no absolution to be had for any of us."

item.title: Riley Gaines' lawsuit vs NCAA dismissed by Biden-appointed judge, appeal planned
item.description: Riley Gaines vows to appeal after a federal judge ruled the NCAA is not subject to Title IX, dismissing her landmark transgender athlete lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A federal judge dismissed Riley Gaines’ lawsuit against the NCAA on Monday after concluding that the evidence did not establish the NCAA as a recipient of federal financial assistance subject to Title IX. Gaines and the Independent Council on Women’s Sports (ICONS) plan to appeal.

Gaines and more than a dozen other current and former female college athletes filed the lawsuit in March 2024, alleging the NCAA violated their Title IX rights by adopting and enforcing policies that permitted biological males to compete in women’s events and use women’s locker rooms.

"This momentary setback will not deter me or other women athletes in the least," Gaines said in a statement. "Rest assured, we will be appealing this decision. We are on the side of truth. I am confident Americans will rally to our side to fight the NCAA."

The plaintiffs have 30 days to file a notice of appeal with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit,

U.S. District Judge Tiffany R. Johnson of the Northern District of Georgia granted the NCAA’s motion for summary judgment on the lawsuit’s remaining Title IX claims. Johnson was nominated to the federal bench by former President Joe Biden in 2024.

Johnson found that the NCAA and the Defense Department maintained separate funding streams for the research. Both contributed money to Indiana University, but the department’s money went to the university and other research participants rather than to the NCAA, according to the order.

The judge also rejected the athletes’ arguments that the NCAA indirectly received federal funding, controlled entities that received the money or became a federal-funding recipient through reimbursements for certain employee travel expenses.

"Here, there is no evidence that the NCAA ever received, or could have received, federal funds," Johnson wrote. "Thus, Plaintiffs’ Title IX claims cannot proceed."

The ruling turned on whether the NCAA qualifies as a recipient of federal financial assistance, a prerequisite for liability under Title IX. It did not decide whether the NCAA’s former transgender-athlete policy constituted sex discrimination.

The case centered heavily on the 2022 NCAA Division I Women’s Swimming and Diving Championships at Georgia Tech, where former University of Pennsylvania swimmer Lia Thomas became the first openly transgender athlete to win an NCAA Division I championship.

Gaines, then swimming for the University of Kentucky, tied Thomas for fifth place in the 200-yard freestyle final. Gaines has also said she and other female swimmers were required to share a locker room with Thomas during the championships.

The lawsuit named athletes from multiple sports, including swimmers Kylee Alons, Reka Gyorgy, Kaitlynn Wheeler and Grace Countie, former San Jose State volleyball player Brooke Slusser and former Roanoke College swimmer Lily Mullens.

Johnson previously dismissed the plaintiffs’ constitutional and bodily-privacy claims, as well as their claims against the University System of Georgia, Georgia Tech and other state defendants. However, in September 2025 she allowed the Title IX claims against the NCAA to survive temporarily, finding that the athletes had plausibly alleged that the organization received federal assistance through a concussion-research partnership with the Department of Defense.

The court then authorized limited discovery specifically addressing the NCAA’s relationship with the Defense Department.

RILEY GAINES AND WOMEN'S SPORTS ACTIVISTS SHARE HONEST REACTIONS, EMOTIONS TO SCOTUS TITLE IX RULING

The decision follows the framework established by the Supreme Court’s 1999 ruling in NCAA v. Smith. In that case, the high court held that the NCAA was not subjected to Title IX merely because it collected dues from member institutions that received federal funds.

ICONS co-founder Kim Jones said the organization believes Johnson erred and predicted the appeals court would conclude that the NCAA, which governs more than 1,100 member colleges and universities, is covered by Title IX.

"We will not give up our fight for women and girls’ rights in sports," Jones said. "ICONS will support an appeal by Riley Gaines, Brooke Slusser, Kylee Alons, Reka Gyorgy, Kaitlynn Wheeler, Grace Countie, Ainsley Erzen, Lily Mullens and the many other young women who depended on the NCAA to protect their equal opportunities but were let down by the NCAA."

The NCAA no longer uses the eligibility policy challenged in the lawsuit. In February 2025, following an executive order from President Donald Trump, the organization changed its rules to prohibit athletes assigned male at birth from competing on women’s teams. Such athletes may still practice with women’s teams and receive certain benefits associated with practicing.

ICONS co-founder Marshi Smith responded to Monday’s decision by urging members of Congress to oppose the Protect College Sports Act, a sweeping bill backed by the NCAA that would establish national rules governing athlete compensation, transfers and eligibility while providing certain antitrust protections to the NCAA, conferences and schools.

The Senate passed the legislation Monday by a 77-22 vote, sending it to the House. The bipartisan proposal is led by Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Maria Cantwell, D-Wash.

"The NCAA’s refusal to recognize its responsibility to uphold women’s rights means the NCAA cannot be trusted to regulate anyone’s sports — men’s or women’s," Smith said.

Smith argued that Congress should not grant the NCAA additional authority after the organization successfully maintained that it was not covered by Title IX.

"The NCAA cannot be trusted to receive broad new powers that it will only use to inflict further harm upon women," she said.

The NCAA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
